capability.summary: Run npm test in a local project and capture its process output
capability.description: Runs exactly `[npm, test]` with cwd set from the explicitly supplied project_dir directory string. The script reads CLI position 1, while the contract intentionally avoids a *_path name so orchestrator file-artifact binding does not misclassify the directory input.
capability.problem_space: Execution of a project's package.json test lifecycle script through npm; not Jest-specific structured reporting, test discovery, dependency installation, advisory auditing, or safe static inspection.

env_requirements: a local npm project whose package.json defines a usable test script and whose dependencies are available
constraint.io_signature: Input: required project_dir string at CLI position 1, explicitly supplied as an existing npm project directory. Because project_dir is kind=string and does not end in *_path, automatic file-artifact binding does not infer this directory. Executes `npm test`. Output: JSON envelope with exit_code and raw streams; no clean field is emitted.
accepted_inputs: an explicitly bound string naming an existing npm project directory whose package.json defines the test lifecycle
constraint.output_shape: npm exit 0 or 1: {status: "success", tool: "npm", target: string, exit_code: 0|1, result: null, stdout: string, stderr: string|null}, wrapper exit 0. Exit 1 may mean test failures or some npm lifecycle/operation errors but still has outer status=success; no clean key exists, so consumers must inspect exit_code and streams. Other npm exits use status="tool_error" and propagate the exit code. Missing target, executable, or 300-second timeout: {status: "error", tool: "npm", message: string}, exiting 2/3/4. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: executes arbitrary commands configured by the project's npm test lifecycle with inherited permissions and environment; tests may modify files, spawn processes, or access networks
does not install dependencies, select a test framework, add npm flags, or parse framework-specific test cases
wraps exit 1 with outer status=success even though it can represent test failures or npm operation errors; because no clean field is emitted, inspect exit_code and stdout/stderr

project_dir is deliberately a plain string contract and does not trigger the orchestrator's *_path file-only heuristic; callers must bind the directory explicitly and automatic artifact binding does not guarantee directory inference
uses a fixed 300-second timeout, captures untruncated stdout/stderr in memory, and is nondeterministic

output_contract.description: JSON npm-test envelope with exit code and raw streams; exit 1 still has outer status=success and no clean field, and project scripts may have side effects.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run the package json npm test script
execute npm tests and capture console output
negative_intents: run Jest with structured Jest JSON results
install npm dependencies or safely inspect tests without execution
